- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of the 30d window).
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias after sharp price spikes in the history (e.g., 35.94, 35.70 → forecast jumps to 38+).
- Model fails to capture mean reversion: after a spike, forecasts remain elevated while true prices often drop or stabilize.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true prices often dip below forecast mid-cycle, suggesting model reacts too slowly to recent volatility.
- Overshoot after spikes: model forecasts peak too high after a price spike, then gradually declines — but not enough to match true price correction.
- Model underestimates volatility in early cycles (e.g., 32.75–33.10 → forecast 33.28–33.36, while true price rises to 35.30).
- Forecast tends to smooth out sharp drops in history, underestimating the magnitude of true price corrections.
- Model exhibits “late correction” bias: true prices often dip below forecast in the last 5–10 days of the 30d window, suggesting model overreacts to recent trends.
